data.body: Make upgrading ddflow in an onboarded project visible, safe and complete. See research R-upgrade-experiment and decision D-upgrade-model (proposed; operator must confirm before tasks start). Generality acceptance for EVERY task: shipped defaults; works on upgrade AND fresh init; tests on throwaway projects including an old-version fixture log (a committed jsonl generated by an old release); no repo-specific references; docs shipped in ddflow/templates; CLI, MCP tool, config knob, README section and all agent integrations (drivers/deltas, MCP instructions, SessionStart hook) updated together.
data.title: ddflow upgrade: detect, plan, back up, apply, repair — on every surface

data.claim: Upgrade is safe for the derived index and for reading old logs (fold is non-strict, index SCHEMA is part of staleness) but there is NO project version stamp, NO skew guard, NO changelog/what-changed view, NO versioned data repairs, and instruction refresh is manual, whole-file and unbacked; so most upgrade effects are silent.
data.falsifier: An old release failing to read a log written by new code, or new code mis-folding an old log, or a stamp/migration mechanism already present.
data.mechanism: State is a pure fold over an append-only log (core/model.fold, strict=False on reads); Store.SCHEMA bump triggers rebuild; Event.schema is written (1) but never checked on read; config loader skips unknown sections with a warning; adopt --refresh-docs copies templates over driver docs; nothing records which ddflow version last wrote the project.
data.probe: Throwaway project in scratchpad/upgrade/proj built with ddflow-mcp 0.1.3 from PyPI (init, adopt claude,codex,gemini, phase + 3 tasks, claims, gates, forced complete, merge, decision, bug, lesson, session prompt/note). Then ran 0.1.10 (PyPI) and main (installed from a worktree) on it: status/doctor/brief/rebuild/config/adopt/adopt --refresh-docs/hooks status; main wrote export.enabled and 0.1.3/0.1.10 read it back; crafted torn line + schema:2 unknown kind + bad-id shard; dangling hook binary; config knob diff and known_kinds diff across the three versions.
data.probe_output: DATA: 0.1.10 and main read the 0.1.3 log with no error; doctor 'index: stale (auto-rebuilds)' (meta schema 8->9). No ddflow version in index meta, events, session.started or config. Event.schema=1 everywhere, never validated on read. Kinds 54 (0.1.3) -> 59 (0.1.10) -> 63 (main), none removed. NEW->OLD: 0.1.3 reads a log with export.enabled silently (status fine, doctor silent on skipped kinds); 0.1.10 doctor notes 'events from a newer ddflow ... skipped: export.enabled x1 (merge main, or run the newer ddflow)' (wrong advice for an installed user: should say upgrade ddflow-mcp). 0.1.3 happily WROTE task T9 into the newer log (no refusal). Config: main wrote [export]; 0.1.3 warns on every command and doctor rc=1 PROBLEM unknown config key; 0.1.3 'config --set' REFUSES ('would break the config: unknown section [export]') so an old agent cannot change config. Indexes rebuild back and forth between versions (harmless). Doctor silent on a FORCED completion (T1 forced over 2 unmet gates: 'Healthy'). Torn line / bad id: doctor PROBLEM forever, no repair verb; recover covers leases only. docs/RECOVERY.md s4: 'There is no migration path and none is needed'. CONFIG: 0.1.3->main: 0 changed defaults of existing knobs but +20 new knobs (14 by 0.1.10: dedupe.*, enforce.readme_*, lease.shared_globs, loops.max_repeated_failures, agent.routers; +6 on main: export.*, mcp.tools). Silent default-on behaviour for old projects: dedupe.on_match was 'warn' in 0.1.9, 'ask' in 0.1.10 (flipped between releases, applies where config.toml has no entry); enforce.readme_with_code=warn; stale_rules=block. `ddflow config` shows [file]/[default] source but no since/changed view; starter config.toml written once by init (stale comments stay). INSTRUCTIONS: doctor does note 'driver docs differ from templates ... adopt --refresh-docs' (byte compare) and 'CLAUDE.md section is from an older version'. adopt --refresh-docs OVERWROTE docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md (shutil.copy2): my appended local line destroyed, no backup, no dry-run, no consent; edit inside the CLAUDE.md managed block destroyed (documented), outside preserved. Driver docs and rules blocks carry NO version/hash header (export docs do: 'ddflow:generated doc= v= body-sha256='; ejected export templates carry a ddflow-shipped digest). Plain adopt re-run also rewrote .mcp.json/.gemini launch entries (path of this install, by design for non-index installs) and added the UserPromptSubmit hook 0.1.3 never installed: new hooks reach old projects only if someone re-runs adopt; hooks status/doctor do not flag missing SessionStart hook. .git/hooks/pre-commit hardcodes the absolute path of the ddflow binary that installed it: with the binary gone EVERY git commit fails 'exec: not found' and neither doctor nor hooks status notices. MCP server loads Config per call but code once; version only in initialize serverInfo; no stale-server detection. Brief staleness note concerns rulebook drift vs main (enforce.stale_rules), not ddflow version. No shipped changelog, but ddflow has the changelog export kind and complete --changelog fields: a ready producer. Past repairs were one-off verbs (session adopt-orphans) or hand data fixes (B-fix-migration-b12-b14); fold fixes repair derived state retroactively for free, wrong data inside events needs corrective events.
data.question: What happens to a ddflow-managed project when ddflow is upgraded (data, config, instructions, features, safety), and what is missing for a safe general upgrade path?

data.body:
New event kind ddflow.seen (data: version, install kind) appended at most once per (agent, version) on first write after a version change, and an explicit upgrade.applied kind (from, to, categories, backup ref); fold keeps highest version seen per project (State.ddflow_versions). Local marker .ddflow/local/seen.json = last version THIS machine acted under. Event.schema is validated on read: schema > known is counted like skipped kinds. Skew guard: a write by a ddflow OLDER than the log's highest stamp is refused (exit 3) with 'upgrade ddflow-mcp to >= X' unless [upgrade].skew = warn; reads always allowed. Fix doctor's skipped-kinds advice to say upgrade ddflow-mcp rather than 'merge main'.
Failing-first: fixture log stamped by a newer version -> current code refuses a write and doctor names versions; old unstamped fixture (generated by 0.1.3, committed under tests/fixtures) reads clean and gets stamped on first write. Old versions skip the new kinds without error (assert via 0.1.3-like fold non-strict). Config knob [upgrade].skew documented in KNOB_DOCS, README, MCP tool description.
data.title: Version stamp and skew detection

data.body:
A machine-readable manifest shipped in the wheel (ddflow/templates/upgrade/changes.toml) listing per release: new knobs (key, default, one-line why), CHANGED defaults (knob, old, new, behaviour effect), instruction/hook/template refreshes, repairs (ids), and opt-in features with the enabling command. Generated at release time from the log's complete --changelog lines + a lint that fails the release when config.py gained/changed a knob not listed (the dedupe warn->ask flip would have been caught). Reader API: changes_since(version).
Failing-first: a test diffs KNOB defaults between the previous tag and HEAD and requires a manifest entry for each added/changed knob; reading since 0.1.3 returns the 20 knobs found in the experiment. Docs shipped in templates; README section.
data.title: Shipped upgrade manifest (what changed since version X)

data.body:
`ddflow upgrade` (default = --plan, writes nothing, exit 0 up to date / 2 nothing to do vs 1 plan pending per exit-code convention), MCP ddflow_upgrade (plan and apply args), and `ddflow doctor --upgrade` as an alias. The plan reports by category: data repairs available, config (new knobs, changed defaults that alter this project's behaviour because it has no entry), instructions (driver docs / rules blocks / native rules whose bytes differ, hand-edited ones flagged separately), hooks (git hooks pointing at a missing or different binary, missing SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks), MCP launch, newly available opt-in features and `ddflow companions`. Reuses driver_drift/rules_status, hooks status, Config source tracking, manifest.
Failing-first: against the 0.1.3-built fixture project the plan lists the missing UserPromptSubmit hook, drifted driver doc, dedupe/readme knobs, a dangling pre-commit binary; against a fresh init it is empty. Plan output byte-identical in CLI --json and MCP.
data.title: ddflow upgrade --plan (dry-run) on CLI, MCP and doctor

data.body:
--apply <category,...>|all. Before ANY write: snapshot every file it will touch to .ddflow/backups/<ts>-<from>-to-<to>/ (local, git-ignored) and print the git diff command; driver docs and rules blocks get a version+body-sha256 header (like export docs) so hand edits are detected and the file is moved aside (.local-edits) or refused, never silently overwritten (also fix adopt --refresh-docs to use it). Dangling git-hook binary is repaired by hooks install. Idempotent: second apply is a no-op. Appends upgrade.applied (from, to, categories, backup) so replay explains it. Config-default changes are never auto-applied: they are listed with 'pin old behaviour: ddflow config --set X old' and recorded when the operator acknowledges.
Failing-first: local edit in driver doc survives to .local-edits and is reported; apply twice = identical tree; kill mid-apply leaves backup and a re-runnable plan; replay shows the upgrade event.
data.title: upgrade --apply: backup, per-category consent, idempotent, recorded

data.body:
A registry of repairs, each {id, since_version, detect(state, log) -> findings, repair(findings) -> corrective events, test fixture}. Run by upgrade/doctor; never rewrites history; applied repairs are recorded (repair.applied id) so they are not re-offered. Seed set from this week's fixes: unadopted orphan prompts/notes (session adopt-orphans), item completed FORCED over unmet gates (report, annotate), shards by an agent with no history, torn/mismatched-id lines (report + quarantine note, no deletion), and stale exported documents carrying an old render (export refresh). Registry rule enforced by a test: a bug closed with a data-damage tag must ship a repair or a documented 'fold-only' note.
Failing-first: a crafted old-version fixture log with each damage kind; detect finds it, repair appends corrective events, second run finds nothing, original lines byte-identical.
data.title: Versioned data repairs (detect, corrective events, test)

data.body:
[upgrade].auto = off | check | safe (shipped default check): check = brief/SessionStart hook/MCP instructions print one line 'ddflow upgraded 0.1.9 -> 0.1.10: run ddflow upgrade --plan' once per machine per version (local seen.json); safe = additionally agents may apply non-destructive categories (backup first); operator-only: config-default changes. Also a stale-server note: MCP server compares its import-time version to the installed dist and the log stamp on each call and says 'restart the server' once. Drivers/deltas and MCP instructions describe the verb for all agents.
Failing-first: simulate version change -> notice appears once, not twice; auto=off prints nothing; safe applies hooks/instructions only; MCP server started under old version emits restart note.
data.title: Session-start upgrade notice and [upgrade].auto policy

data.body: README upgrade section (what is silent, what is consented, downgrade/rollback via backups + git, two-version skew rules, shard union-merge); fix RECOVERY.md 'no migration path' wording; drivers mention ddflow upgrade. End-to-end test: committed fixture project generated by an old release (tests/fixtures/<ver>/ with populated log) goes through plan -> apply -> doctor Healthy -> replay on throwaway tmp dirs; same test on fresh init expects empty plan; no repo-specific references (grep test).
data.title: Docs and an end-to-end old-to-new upgrade test

data.alternatives: Schema migrations of the log (rejected: append-only, rewriting history). Silent auto-refresh at every start (rejected: overwrites local edits, surprises operator). Doing nothing but doctor notes (status quo).
data.consequences: New event kinds (old ddflow skips them with a note); one more verb and knob; release process must maintain the manifest (lint enforces); skew guard can refuse an old ddflow's writes.
data.context: Experiment R-upgrade-experiment: reads of old logs are safe, but there is no stamp, skew guard, changelog, repair registry; adopt --refresh-docs destroys local edits; default flips (dedupe warn->ask) and new hooks reach old projects silently; a dangling hook binary blocks every commit unnoticed.
data.decision: Add `ddflow upgrade` (plan by default; --apply per category; MCP ddflow_upgrade; doctor --upgrade) built on: (1) a shared version stamp (ddflow.seen / upgrade.applied events) plus a local last-seen marker; (2) a changelog/manifest shipped in the wheel; (3) backups under .ddflow/backups before any write and managed-file headers with version+body-sha256; (4) a registry of versioned, idempotent data repairs that append corrective events only; (5) [upgrade].auto = off|check|safe. History is never rewritten and the index stays disposable (no schema migrations).
data.title: Upgrade model: stamped log, shipped manifest, dry-run plan, consented categories, versioned repairs
